citation.title: AI Moral Enhancement: Upgrading the Socio-Technical System of Moral Engagement

reading.source_scope_note: Conceptual/normative proposal for multiple AI dialogue tools representing wisdom traditions, supporting users’ own practical judgment rather than replacing it. No system evaluation, new participant sample, controlled educational outcome or measured safeguard effectiveness reported.
access_limits: All supplied text and references read; no substantive visual appendix or public supplementary material identified. No raw data, executable prototype or user study reported for this proposal.

Haidt,Hume,Nussbaum,Mill,Boden,Dreyfus and other books/articles are cited or quoted, not independently fully read. Do not count book quotations, blog examples or reference metadata as additional full-source reviews.

Socratic-assistant originals by Lara/Deckers and Lara, classroom education evidence, ProjectDebater, Dennett-style language models and game-playing systems were not independently fully read or reproduced through this bibliography.
The authors explicitly call actual educational sufficiency an empirical matter. Claims that modularity minimizes disengagement or ensures pluralism remain proposed benefits, not observed guarantees.

study.design: Philosophical critique and design proposal. Distinguishes exhaustive moral enhancement that supplants human judgment from auxiliary assistance, then proposes plural modules as interactive book-like interlocutors. These are design stances rather than new experimental conditions.
study.criterion: Proposed success concerns a learner’s clarity,cogency,profundity and sensitivity in continuing ethical inquiry. No validated scoring rubric, baseline, longitudinal retention, behavioral outcome or proof of morally better decisions supplied.
study.reasoning: Accurate outputs, consistency,speed and efficiency do not by themselves establish moral improvement. Context, affect, practical experience and public contestation are argued to matter. The paper does not categorically deny that AI might model practical wisdom, and it presents game-to-morality transfer conditionally rather than as a proven equivalence.
study.socratic_method: AI-supported dialogue offers empirical support,conceptual clarification,argument testing,awareness of limitations and practical guidance. Authors challenge neutrality claims and propose distinct traditions/points of view, with the user retaining judgment and control.
study.modularity: A library-like diversity of interlocutors is a proposed architecture, not proof of independent evidence or comprehensive fair representation. Shared model/training biases, module selection, unequal access and covert steering require evaluation. This paper is not an instruction to deploy agents or contact anyone.
study.mentoring_boundary: Authors explicitly say AI mentors are tools,not genuine mentors,and should not be mistaken for people. Style imitation or expert confusion is not proof of practical wisdom, reciprocal care, consciousness or trustworthy teaching.
study.claims_and_limits: Moral disengagement/deskilling are proposed risks of outsourced judgment; plural dialogue is a proposed response. No measured prevention effect or guarantee that more perspectives always improve decisions. The authors acknowledge possible confusion,dead ends and aporia.

summary: Add Socratic dialogue as a reasoning/education method. Enrich practical wisdom,moral deskilling,disengagement and dumbfounding with source-specific conceptual boundaries. Keep auxiliary/exhaustive enhancement,modularity and transcendence as design/philosophical distinctions rather than inflate behavior counts. Correct a verified author spelling and truncated source locator; no empirical guarantee or unread-book credit.

findings.definition: Using questions and reasoned dialogue to clarify concepts, test assumptions and develop a person’s own judgment.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Proposed AI-assisted educational method; no evaluated intervention in this article
findings.novelty_rationale: A structured inquiry method that develops the participant’s reasoning rather than merely giving a verdict, assigning an opposing advocate, comparing cases or seeking counterevidence. Existing practical wisdom is a capacity/goal; dialogue is a proposed means of cultivating it.

evidence.quote: help the agent to learn to reason ethically

findings.evidence_scope: The authors extend Socratic-assistant proposals into a plural library of tradition-specific AI interlocutors. Educational benefits and protection against disengagement are argued, not measured. The source explicitly recognizes that adequacy for developing human practical judgment is an empirical question.
findings.boundary: Questioning is not automatically neutral, accurate or beneficial. It can conceal steering, reproduce bias or burden users. Match the authorized task: do not withhold a requested direct answer or impose endless questions. Disagreement and unresolved inquiry do not prove failure; agreement with a module does not prove moral improvement.
findings.ai_proposal: For a user who requests reflective learning, have an assistant ask relevant clarifying/testing questions, represent alternative arguments accurately and leave judgments reviewable. Evaluate independent reasoning, transfer and later unaided performance against a direct-answer baseline, while measuring burden and unwanted steering.

findings.definition: Context-sensitive judgment that integrates relevant knowledge, values and particular circumstances to decide what should be done.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; retain the philosophical argument and proposed educational use without claiming a new empirical effect.

evidence.quote: cultivate the users’ own practical wisdom

findings.evidence_scope: Practical wisdom is framed as context-sensitive human judgment developed through experience,discussion and training. Proposed outcomes include clarity,cogency,profundity and sensitivity rather than compliance with an AI oracle. No validation of a learner improvement metric is reported.
findings.boundary: A thoughtful style,plural discussion or tradition label does not establish sound judgment. The paper allows the possibility of AI modeling wisdom but demonstrates neither AI wisdom nor a safe educational effect.

findings.definition: Erosion of ethical judgment or sensitivity through repeatedly delegating morally consequential decisions rather than exercising that competence.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; retain the philosophical argument and proposed educational use without claiming a new empirical effect.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper argues that reliance on moral technology may erode the skills needed to evaluate or correct it, motivating participatory education. This is a philosophical risk argument citing prior work, not a new longitudinal study.
findings.boundary: Authorized assistance can preserve or improve competence. Repeated dialogue,slower responses or disagreement do not by themselves show upskilling or loss of moral skill; actual unaided transfer and context-sensitive outcomes need measurement.

findings.definition: Suspending or bypassing moral self-regulation so harmful conduct can be justified before or after it occurs.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; retain the philosophical argument and proposed educational use without claiming a new empirical effect.
findings.evidence_scope: The authors connect AI-oracle obedience and narrow economic deflection to risks of moral disengagement,then propose dialogue to preserve agency. This is conceptual analysis,not an experiment showing a measured disengagement mechanism.
findings.boundary: Legitimate delegation and justified reliance are not automatically disengagement. Multiple modules do not guarantee prevention or neutral advice; no inferred model guilt,intent or moral feeling.

findings.definition: Holding a firm moral verdict while unable to give reasons for it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Existing construct; retain the philosophical argument and proposed educational use without claiming a new empirical effect.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper recounts Haidt’s moral-dumbfounding examples: a firm intuitive verdict persists despite failed articulated reasons. These are secondary accounts used to motivate intellectual humility and dialogue; the original experiments and book are not independently fully read.
findings.boundary: Failure to articulate reasons is not proof that no reason exists or that a moral verdict is wrong. A model’s unsupported judgment or post-hoc explanation does not demonstrate a human intuitive emotional state. Cultural explanations and the correct moral answer are not settled by this conceptual source.

methodological_limits: No new experiment,implemented system,systematic review or causal training test. Proposed safeguards and improvement criteria remain to be evaluated.
Moral correctness,reasoning quality,pluralism,user control and agreement are distinct. A diversity of personas can share biases and omit important perspectives.
Historical/philosophical claims and secondary psychology/game-playing/blog examples are not independent primary validations of the proposal.
Dialogue may support judgment but can also overwhelm or covertly steer. It needs task fit,accurate evidence,transparent perspective and genuine user choice.
Books and AI tools need not be full moral agents to assist education; useful interactivity does not establish real mentorship,consciousness or reciprocal duty.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Both papers warn against moral abdication,but this proposal leaves open AI modeling of wisdom and emphasizes plural dialogue. Preserve their different philosophical positions rather than declare machine moral capacity empirically settled.
Education needs outcomes beyond positive attitudes or intentions. This article proposes richer dialogical criteria but does not test them or demonstrate clinical/real-world ethical improvement.
More reflection and time do not automatically yield more accurate or justified moral judgments. A Socratic format needs actual process and outcome evidence rather than a dual-process label.

deferred.reason: Design goals concerning support versus replacement of human judgment,not separately demonstrated psychological behaviors. Retain their definitions and tradeoff in this review.
Normative and architectural commitments in the proposal; no independent process or validated behavioral outcome justifies new records here.
Philosophical aspirations and functional metaphors. Authors explicitly distinguish tools from genuine mentors; do not infer subjectivity or empirical moral superiority.

limitations: One reasoning method added. Normative proposal and secondary source discussion remain labeled; no unread-book credits,proven mentor efficacy,independent-agent guarantee,fabricated annual counts or automatic harm/principle edges.
